hints: At a constant horizontal speed, acceleration is zero, so the driving force of the engines equals the resistance force.
Convert power from kilowatts to watts and resistance from kilonewtons to newtons ($P = 5\,500\,000\text{ W}$, $F = 25\,000\text{ N}$).
Use the power formula $P = F v$ and solve for the speed $v$.
walkthrough:
Since the aeroplane flies at constant speed in horizontal motion, the driving force equals the resistance force:
$$F = 25\text{ kN} = 25\,000\text{ N}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Because the aeroplane travels horizontally at a constant speed, its acceleration is zero. By Newton's first law, the forward driving force $F_D$ produced by the engines must exactly balance the backward resistance force $R$:
$$F_D = R = 25\text{ kN} = 25\,000\text{ N}$$

Convert the given engine power from kilowatts to standard SI units (watts):
$$P = 5500\text{ kW} = 5500 \times 1000 = 5\,500\,000\text{ W}$$

Recall the formula relating power, driving force, and speed:
$$P = F_D \times v$$

Substitute the known values into the formula:
$$5\,500\,000 = 25\,000 \times v$$

Rearrange to solve for $v$ by dividing both sides by $25\,000$:
$$v = \frac{5\,500\,000}{25\,000} = \frac{5500}{25} = 220\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

ai_rubric.Using Power and Resistance Relationships: Equates driving force to $25000\text{ N}$, applies $P = Fv$ with $5500000 = 25000v$, and solves to find $v = 220\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

hints: Since the aeroplane maintains the same constant speed, its kinetic energy does not change ($\Delta KE = 0$).
Apply the work-energy principle: Work done by engines = Increase in gravitational potential energy + Work done against resistance.
Calculate the change in potential energy using $\Delta PE = mgh$, add the work against resistance to obtain the total work, then divide by time to find average power.
walkthrough:
Calculate the gain in gravitational potential energy during the $300\text{ m}$ ascent:
$$\Delta PE = mgh = 60\,000 \times 10 \times 300 = 180\,000\,000\text{ J} = 180\,000\text{ kJ}$$

Express the work done by the engines over $50\text{ s}$ in terms of average power $P$:
$$W_{\text{engines}} = P \times t = 50P$$

Form the three-term work-energy equation, noting that kinetic energy is constant ($\Delta KE = 0$):
$$W_{\text{engines}} = \Delta PE + W_{\text{resistance}}$$
$$50P = 180\,000\,000 + 270\,000\,000 = 450\,000\,000\text{ J}$$

Solve for the average power $P$:
$$P = \frac{450\,000\,000}{50} = 9\,000\,000\text{ W} = 9000\text{ kW}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
State the work-energy principle for a powered system. Because the aeroplane maintains a constant speed, the change in kinetic energy is zero ($\Delta KE = 0$). Therefore, all the work done by the engines goes into increasing gravitational potential energy and overcoming resistive forces:
$$W_{\text{engines}} = \Delta PE + W_{\text{resistance}}$$

Calculate the increase in gravitational potential energy using $\Delta PE = mgh$, where $m = 60\,000\text{ kg}$, $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, and $h = 300\text{ m}$:
$$\Delta PE = 60\,000 \times 10 \times 300 = 180\,000\,000\text{ J} = 180\,000\text{ kJ}$$

The work done against resistance is given as $270\,000\text{ kJ} = 270\,000\,000\text{ J}$. Find the total work done by the engines:
$$W_{\text{engines}} = 180\,000\,000 + 270\,000\,000 = 450\,000\,000\text{ J}$$

Recall that average power is the total work done divided by the time elapsed:
$$P = \frac{W_{\text{engines}}}{t}$$

Substitute $W_{\text{engines}} = 450\,000\,000\text{ J}$ and $t = 50\text{ s}$ into the power formula:
$$P = \frac{450\,000\,000}{50} = 9\,000\,000\text{ W}$$

Convert the answer to kilowatts:
$$P = \frac{9\,000\,000}{1000} = 9000\text{ kW}$$
